chunks: Al-ʿAlāʾ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

Regarding two men, each of whom had food with his companion, and neither of them knew how much he had with his companion, each of them said to the other: “What is with you is yours, and what is with me is mine.”
So he عليه السلام said: “There is no harm in that if they both mutually agree and their souls are content.”

key_terms.تَرَاضَيَا: they mutually agreed and were satisfied
key_terms.صَاحِبِهِ: his companion or counterpart in the transaction
key_terms.طَابَتْ أَنْفُسُهُمَا: both felt inwardly content and willing
key_terms.طَعَامٌ: food property held or stored with another person
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for two people to settle exchanged goods when the exact amounts are unknown if both agree?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about mutual settlement when two people each hold property for the other but do not know the exact amounts. Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام permits the arrangement so long as both parties are mutually satisfied and willingly consent.
